types.oie_definition: A sovereign state or nation.
types.embedding_query_text: Country: A sovereign state or nation. Also called nation, state, realm, land.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org 'Country' class perfectly matches the OIE type definition and mentions.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

candidates.label: Landform
candidates.comment: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.

candidates.label: BodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A Landform representing a significant accumulation of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake. Also called aquatic environment, water body, large water mass. Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

types.oie_definition: An organized competition or series of competitions in sports.
types.embedding_query_text: Sporting Event: An organized competition or series of competitions in sports. Also called sports competition, tournament, championship, games.

chosen_type.label: SportsEvent
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org 'SportsEvent' class perfectly matches the OIE type definition and mention.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

types.oie_definition: A large and permanent human settlement.
types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and permanent human settlement. Also called metropolis, town, urban center, municipality.

candidates.label: City

Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

types.oie_definition: A specific day of the year.

candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

types.oie_definition: A length of time.
types.embedding_query_text: Duration: A length of time. Also called period, span, interval, time frame.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org 'Duration' class perfectly matches the OIE type definition and mention.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: InstantaneousEvent
candidates.comment: An InstantaneousEvent is a structured value representing an event with no duration, such as a single point in time. Also called momentary event, point event, discrete occurrence. Examples: a computer log entry, a timestamp, a single click on a webpage. Distinct from Event, which typically has a duration.

types.oie_definition: A specific point or period within a 24-hour day.
types.embedding_query_text: Time of Day: A specific point or period within a 24-hour day. Also called time, part of day, moment.

chosen_type.label: DayPeriod
chosen_type.definition: A specific point or period within a 24-hour day.
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org 'Time' is too precise for descriptive periods like 'morning' or 'night'; no existing type fits these natural language periods.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

types.oie_definition: A broad road or street, often lined with trees.
types.embedding_query_text: Avenue: A broad road or street, often lined with trees. Also called boulevard, street, thoroughfare, road.

chosen_type.label: Street
chosen_type.definition: A public road in a city or town.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org type for a 'street' or 'avenue'; candidates are all incorrect.

candidates.label: Canal
candidates.comment: An artificial waterway constructed for navigation, irrigation, or drainage. Also called waterway, artificial channel, navigation channel. Examples: Panama Canal, Suez Canal, Erie Canal, Grand Canal of China.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: Beach
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure consisting of a sandy or pebbly shore by a body of water. Also called seashore, coastline, sandy beach, waterfront. Examples: "Copacabana Beach", "Malibu Beach", "Waikiki Beach".

candidates.label: RiverBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A natural flowing watercourse, typically freshwater, flowing towards an ocean, sea, lake, or another river. Also called river, stream, waterway, current. Examples: the Nile River, the Amazon River, the Mississippi River, the Thames. Distinct from SeaBodyOfWater, which is a large expanse of saltwater.

candidates.label: BodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A Landform representing a significant accumulation of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake. Also called aquatic environment, water body, large water mass. Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

types.oie_definition: A printed publication containing news, articles, advertisements, and correspondence.
types.embedding_query_text: Newspaper: A printed publication containing news, articles, advertisements, and correspondence. Also called journal, gazette, paper, daily.

chosen_type.label: Newspaper
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org 'Newspaper' class perfectly matches the OIE type definition and mention.

candidates.label: Newspaper
candidates.comment: A Newspaper, as a Periodical, is a publication containing information about varied topics, often published daily. Also called daily paper, news publication, gazette. Examples: The Wall Street Journal, The Guardian, a local community newspaper. Distinct from Magazine, which is typically published weekly or monthly with a specific focus.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

candidates.label: Article
candidates.comment: An Article is a CreativeWork, typically a written piece such as a news report, magazine feature, or investigative report. Also called written piece, report, feature, essay, column. Examples: a newspaper article about local politics, a magazine feature on travel, a scientific journal article, a blog post. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is a specific type of article published on a blog.

candidates.label: Periodical
candidates.comment: A Periodical, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a publication issued in successive parts with numerical or chronological designations, intended to continue indefinitely. Also called serial publication, magazine, journal. Examples: The New Yorker magazine, a scholarly journal, a daily newspaper. Distinct from Book, which is a single, non-serial publication.

types.oie_definition: An online service or website that allows users to create and share content or to participate in social networking.
types.embedding_query_text: Social Media Platform: An online service or website that allows users to create and share content or to participate in social networking. Also called social network, online community, digital platform.

chosen_type.label: SocialMediaPlatform
chosen_type.definition: An online service or website that allows users to create and share content or to participate in social networking.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org type specifically represents a 'social media platform' as a service or organization; 'DigitalPlatformEnumeration' is for generic platform types.

candidates.label: SocialMediaPosting
candidates.comment: A creative work published on a social media platform, such as a blog post, tweet, or Facebook update. Also called social post, microblog post, status update, online share. Examples: a tweet from a celebrity, a Facebook status update, a blog post on Medium, an Instagram caption.

candidates.label: DiscussionForumPosting
candidates.comment: A social media posting that is an entry or message within an online discussion forum. Also called Forum post, message board entry, thread reply, online discussion. Examples: A question posted on a tech support forum, a comment in a gaming community thread, a new topic started on a hobby board. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically a longer, standalone article on a blog.

candidates.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration listing common technology platforms, used to specify where an action or content is available. Also called Technology platform, software platform, operating system, device type. Examples: iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, Console. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is the application itself, not the platform it runs on.

candidates.label: BlogPosting
candidates.comment: An Article that is an individual entry or post published within a blog. Also called blog post, blog entry, weblog post. Examples: "A blog post about new software features", "An article on a travel blog", "A recipe post on a food blog". Distinct from Blog, which is the collection of posts.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.
